#4260. Nearly 3 in 4 Gamers Are More Likely to Wait for Sales, Newzoo and G2A Find

A Montreal-based Game enthusiast who has been writing about the industry since 2013.

Price and gaming has taken on an entirely new meaning over the last year. The idea of waiting for a sale became a borderline meme over a decade ago, when Steam started running infamous deep-discount sales on digital games. A cursory search for “Gabe” or “Steam Sale” can be a long timetraveling road through years of in-jokes from the enthusiast community. These goofs and gags barely hold up all these years later, but they do harken back to a simpler time in the world of games pricing.

Today, conversations around discounts, sales, and pricing will launch just about anyone from the wide-world of gaming into a tirade about a whole host of criticism of the game industry: what do we do about physical games, do we even own digital games, is Mario Kart World worth X number of dollars. The list goes on. In the market of 2026, between the cost of individual games, the increasing price of hardware, live-service games, and monthly subscriptions, there are more factors than ever that influence player spending habits. It’s a fascinating time to look into how pricing dynamics are influencing the industry.

A report from Newzoo and G2A.COM found that 73% of surveyed players say they are more likely to wait for sales these days. The survey included 6,166 active PC or console players aged 18–55 across six countries, all of whom had purchased or played at least one AAA or AA game in the previous year. The study, “Game purchasing behavior in an era of choice” investigates how modern PC and console players are choosing to spend their hard-earned money in 2026. And while, yes, most players are happy to let the release date come and go so they can get a good deal on a given game, that doesn’t mean that players are entirely content to wait particularly long for a discount.

Wardogs lead developer Joe Brammer took to X (formerly Twitter) to offer another perspective on why studios are struggling to stay afloat.

Looking back at their purchases over the past three years, respondents reported buying just 42% of games before or during release month: 17% through pre-orders and 25% during the month itself. So how does this break down outside of the launch window?

In summary, of the purchases respondents recalled making over the past three years, 82% happened before release or within a game’s first year, including pre-orders. The remaining 18% happened more than a year after release. Crucially, it’s worth bearing in mind that this describes the timing of reported purchases. Still, it highlights how important it is for publishers keep a game top-of-mind after launch, and make sure players are able to take advantage of discounts and other offers post-launch.

Among players who buy beyond release month, the average expected wait for a discount worth considering is 4.9 months. And naturally, how deep the discount cuts plays a big role in purchasing behaviour.

On average, respondents consider a game reasonably priced at 29% off, and Newzoo notes that a 45% discount represents a ‘good deal.’ In their sample, audiences considered a 70% cut a potential red flag to a game’s quality, which is an interesting note that’s hard to unsee when you browse Steam.

Now's your chance to save 50% on one of the best releases of the summer.

One of the other notable data points from the study is that despite players being happy to wait for discounts, they also consider games a very high-value medium. In fact, 69% consider it better value than entertainment such as television, films and music, while 62% agree that game prices reflect rising development costs and complexity. Of course, that doesn’t mean audiences aren’t always still looking for a deal if they can take advantage of one.

“With nearly 60% of purchases occurring later than release month, publishers need long-term monetisation strategies that go well beyond the first week or month,” Newzoo research director Alexis Pamboris said in the press release.

Where people shop is another piece of the puzzle. Official digital storefronts (PSN, Steam, etc.) are expectedly dominant, but 24% of subjects in the study claim to use third-party marketplaces to purchase or research a title. G2A, which co-authored the report and runs its own marketplace, states that the alternate purchasing channels give players more choice. As stated by G2A chief business officer Katarzyna Jakubiec, “different purchasing channels serve different consumer needs.”

Most players, especially those with a Steam backlog, can probably relate to some of Newzoo and G2A’s findings. Waiting for a sale is a familiar part of deciding what to buy, from a box of cereal to a piping-hot copy of Grand Theft Auto VI. What’s interesting is how clearly that patience shows up in the numbers. Players still want new games, but many are willing to let release day pass until the price feels right. For publishers, the challenge is giving them a reason to finally move something from the wishlist to the library.

For a full deep-dive on all that findings inside Newzoo and G2A's report, you can visit their site here.

#4259. Vampirio is a rogue-like action RPG that lets you build by day and slay monsters at night — here are 5 reasons to sink your teeth into it

Outfit7, the publisher behind Talking Tom & Friends, has just launched Vampirio, a rogue-like action RPG that combines monster-slaying combat with fortress-building and nightly survival battles. Here are five reasons to take a closer look. A familiar character…with a twist Before there was Dracula, there was Vlad Dracul, a young monster hunter whose life is torn apart by loss. Vampirio explores the events that set him on a path of vengeance toward becoming the legendary vampire.

You’ll discover his story while battling waves of monsters in a vibrant, top-down world. With different playable heroes and rogue-like progression adding variety to each run, there’s more to surviving the night than simply slaying everything in sight.

Nine heroes, different ways to fight Vampirio features nine playable heroes, each bringing different abilities and a distinct combat style.

The first hero you’ll play is Alba, who introduces you to the fundamentals before more heroes become available. As you unlock characters including Vlad, Lucian, and Morana, experiment to find the playstyles that suit you.

Whether you prefer ranged attacks, close-range combat, or powerful magic, switching heroes can change how you approach a fight and which upgrades you choose.

Brains over brawn Surviving monster-filled nights requires more than a strong roster of heroes, and this is where Vampirio’s base-building elements come into play.

During the day, gather resources, expand your fortress, and build or upgrade walls and defensive towers. When night falls, those preparations are put to the test as your hero fights alongside your defences.

From skeletons to dragons and powerful bosses, each night brings fresh threats to overcome. Careful preparation can make the difference between holding the line and watching your defences crumble.

Rogue-like progression Every run offers opportunities to experiment with different skills and upgrades, encouraging you to adapt your strategy as the challenge unfolds. Randomised upgrades keep encounters fresh, meaning you can't rely on the same approach every time.

That doesn't mean you're starting from scratch after every defeat, though. Permanent progression gives you ways to grow stronger between runs, while developing your heroes adds another layer of long-term strategy,

You’ll also collect enemy stickers by defeating monsters and bosses. Completing sticker collections unlocks lasting progression bonuses, giving you another way to strengthen future runs.

Raid rival fortresses — and risk revenge Not all your resource-gathering has to happen at home. Vampirio also lets you raid other players' fortresses, offering another way to gather supplies.

Destroying buildings and looting resources can help you climb the lifetime rankings, but there's a catch: your targets can retaliate with revenge attacks. Raiding therefore comes with a risk, especially when you already have your hands full defending against the creatures of the night.

You'll need to weigh the rewards against the potential consequences as you decide how aggressively to expand your resources and strengthen your fortress.

Vampirio is available to download now on iOS, Android and Steam. As an extra bit of fun, you can also find out which hero matches you best by taking the Vampirio personality quiz: https://vampirio.app/quiz

#4257. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4256. Vampirio beginner’s guide - 10 tips and tricks to help you survive Outfit7’s monster-slaying RPG

Vampirio is Outfit7’s new rogue-like action RPG, combining fast-paced survival combat with strategic base-building. Prepare your fortress by day, then take control of heroes with different abilities and combat styles to defend it at night. Alongside the battles, the story explores Vlad Dracul’s journey toward becoming Dracula. With so many RPG games out there, could Vampirio make your top 10? The day offers sanctuary, a time when you can fortify your territory, gather resources, build new defences, upgrade existing buildings, and repair damage inflicted the previous night. Use this opportunity to its fullest and don’t waste time waiting for the battle to start.

When night falls it’ll be too late to fix what you’ve neglected. You’re fighting with the fortress you built and there are no refunds. 2. Don’t upgrade everything equally

Always remember that resources are limited so spreading them evenly across your fortress isn’t always the best strategy.

Before spending anything, take some time to ask yourself: what went wrong the night before? Where were your enemies breaching defences faster than other areas?

When rebuilding, we suggest you focus your efforts on these points. The day offers a window of opportunity in Vampirio, one where monsters aren’t trying to eat you, so use it wisely. 3. Keep moving Staying on the move is an essential tactic. Watch where enemies are approaching from, create space, and reposition before you’re surrounded. Getting trapped between monsters and your own defences can quickly spell disaster.

Also remember that you’re defending your fortress as well as keeping your hero alive. Watch for areas under pressure and be ready to move where your help is needed most. 4. Stay involved in the fight During battles, your hero levels up, gains skills, and develops a build for that run. Stay involved by clearing enemies, creating space, and supporting defences that are coming under pressure.

Balance aggression with positioning. Look for opportunities to attack, but don’t charge into a situation you can’t get out of. Staying effective matters more than chasing every enemy. 5. Stop waiting for the perfect build It pays to remember that rogue-like progression means you won't always get the upgrade you're hoping for. Rather than chasing the same perfect build every run, learn to work with the options you're given.

Before choosing your next upgrade, take stock of your current abilities. Does an option shore up a weakness, strengthen a strategy that's already working, or give you a new way to deal with the problem at hand?

Keep this in mind as you play Vampirio: the strongest build isn't necessarily the one you planned, but the one you learn to make work. 6. More damage isn’t always the answer A good offence can help you win the battle, but a strong defence is essential to winning the war. When choosing upgrades, consider what your current situation demands rather than automatically opting for more damage.

If your health is running low and enemies are overwhelming your position, improving your survivability or ability to hold back the horde could be more valuable than another offensive boost. Sometimes, staying alive is the best strategy. 7. Don't chase kills while your fortress burns It's easy to get tunnel vision when you're surrounded by enemies. But while you're busy taking down the monsters in front of you, other threats could be putting your fortress in danger elsewhere.

Don't let the thrill of combat distract you from the bigger picture. Keep checking your surroundings, pay attention to where enemies are gathering, and be ready to break away from a fight if your defences need help. A kill isn't worth much if your fortress falls while you're chasing it. 8. Learn with Alba – then learn again

Alba helps introduce you to Vampirio's fundamentals, giving you a starting point as you learn to survive its nightly assaults. But don't assume that the same tactics will work equally well with every hero.

As you unlock heroes such as Vlad, Lucian, and Morana, experiment with their different abilities and combat styles. Pay attention to how each one changes your approach to a fight, and choose upgrades that complement their strengths.

The more familiar you become with your roster, the better equipped you'll be to adapt your strategy to whatever the night throws at you. 9. If a boss breaks your strategy, let it

A strategy that handles regular enemy waves with ease might struggle when a boss arrives.

When that happens don't panic and simply try to do more of what worked before. Instead, take the time to observe how the boss moves and attacks.

Look for moments when your usual positioning or tactics stop working, then adjust accordingly. You might need to change where you fight, rethink your approach or prioritise survival over dealing damage.

Preparation is essential, but adaptation is what gets you through the toughest encounters. 10. One bad night isn't the whole game A bad run in Vampirio doesn't have to mean your time’s been wasted. Every attempt gives you an opportunity to learn what worked, identify what went wrong and approach the next challenge more effectively.

Vampirio also features long-term progression through heroes, gear, and permanent upgrades, giving you more ways to grow stronger beyond individual runs.

Take stock of your heroes and upgrades, rethink your battle plan, and make any necessary preparations before heading out again. Each run is another chance to improve, experiment and discover a strategy that works.

So don't let one disastrous night put you off. Learn from it, regroup and get ready for the next sunset.

#4254. TYLOO’s Lisbon forfeit dents Singapore Major hopes as 100 Thieves edge out fnatic

TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

#4253. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4250. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4249. 10 Legendary Shields You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Legendary items are the prize you are searching for in Borderlands 4. They will help you complete your build, and carry you into the different levels of Mayhem Mode.

With over a year’s worth of content added to the game, there are plenty of legendary items, which means you need to start refining which ones are best for your characters. Once you have all your legendary weapons, including legendary assault rifles, you need to move on to legendary shields.

Shields will protect you, give you some additional buffs, and help you fight back against the swarms of psychos and Order Troops across Kairos. If you haven’t obtained them already, these shields are ones that you should definitely get.

One of the best shields from the base game of Borderlands 4 is the Super Soldier, as it literally enhances your abilities, turning you into someone who can run and shoot fast. It is almost like you took the super serum given to Captain America. There are plenty of references and easter eggs to find across Kairos, too.

The shield has the ability called Power Play, which gives you an overshield whenever the shield refills. This is great for procing abilities on weapons like the Ohm I got that get benefits from overshields.

Additionally, while your shield is full, it grants you 25% increased fire rate and 25% increased movement speed, which is amazing on characters like Rafa and Loveless who can amp up their movement speed. If you want to get this shield, you will need to farm Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

There are some shields that will carry you far into the game, and then there are shields that are perfect starting shields that pack a punch, and are great for new characters. The Firewerks shield is perfect for any new character that you create.

This shield comes with the Bundled ability, which fires rockets at enemies each time you get a kill. These missiles deal fairly decent damage, making it easier to clear crowds of enemies quickly.

Of course, being a shield you want to get early, you would expect to be able to farm this weapon early in the game, which you can. You can get this shield from Spashzone in Riptide Grotto, which is near where you start the game. Some legendary farming locations are trickier to find than you may think.

A shield is meant to keep you safe from damage, and the Onion is all about that by offering you a means of negating damage for brief periods of time. Instead of a normal shield, this is an armor shield, meaning it has multiple segments.

The ability Shallot Shell makes it so you are immune to damage for a couple seconds after an armor segment breaks. Since this shield often has four segments, you have four times where you will be immune to damage before the shield is gone.

It is great for increasing your survivability, and is perfect for characters who are a bit squishy. You can obtain this shield by farming Sludgemaw at Watershed Gate.

How do Borderlands 4's new Vault Hunters stack up?

Do you want a shield that will cause some devastation each time it breaks and refills? Well, you might want to get your hands on the Extra Medium then, as it will cause some serious devastation.

This shield isn’t the most protective, with it sitting near the average when it comes to shield health. However, this is made up for by the ability Nucleosynthesis, which causes it to trigger a nova that deals major damage in the surrounding area each time it breaks or refills.

Of course, you need to let the shield completely refill before you can trigger the effect again, but it is great for getting out of sticky situations, and you can obtain this shield by farming the Vault Boss named Inceptus.

One of the biggest things that kills me in Borderlands 4 is self-damage. I blow myself up all the time with grenades and other types of splash damage. It is a serious issue. Luckily, the Honey Badger fixes this issue.

The Honey Badger shield has the Ferocity ability, which reduces self-damage dealt by 90%, meaning you can take a hit from a grenade and not get thrown into a fight for your life. It is the perfect shield for those who deal a lot of splash damage all around them with Torgue weapons.

Of course, if you don’t have this issue, you can skip over this shield, but it is worth it if you do. You can get the Honey Badger from Big Oil in the Bloodstained Hollow as part of the Vault of the Damned DLC. For more gear, check out the best DLC weapons.

There are some shields that have amazing abilities that boost your damage, but this damage buff comes at a cost. For the Protean Cell, this cost is the shield’s health. Luckily, it has a lot of health.

This shield has the Direct Current ability, which drains the shield over time, but grants you a bonus 40% shock damage. However, while this ability is active, you take direct damage, meaning the shield won’t protect you, so you need to be selective about when you use it.

Use this shield correctly, and you will rip through enemy health bars in seconds. Just don’t get carried away or it could mean the end of your character. You can get this shield from Fractis in Grindstone of the Worthy.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Every character can have some sort of status effect build, which makes the Exfoliatrix a great shield because it can be used efficiently by every character. You just need to be running a status effect build.

The ability of this shield is Exfoliatrix, which increases your status effect chance for six seconds each time an armor segment breaks. Additionally, whenever an enemy receives status effect damage, you recover a portion of the shield.

If you are constantly dealing status effect damage, you will be well protected by this shield, and you won’t need to worry about taking damage. You can get this shield by farming the Digi-Rifts on Providence Island in the FL4K and the Last Resort DLC.

An interesting ability that some shields have is that they can spawn kill drones that help you damage enemies. The Little Sister is one of these shields, and it does a great job taking down enemies.

It has the ability Sister, which grants you a kill drone whenever an armor segment breaks. This kill drone fights alongside you, mimicking the element of the gun you are using, and dealing 25% of the gun’s damage.

It is a perfect little partner to help you on the battlefield, and one that will continuously deal damage for you, helping you to wipe out groups of enemies. You can get this shield from Throne’s Experiments in Research Center B-0451. It can also be dropped from the chests at the end of the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

The Watts 4 Dinner shield is pretty similar to the Protean Cell shield, as they both grant you bonus shock damage. While the damage buff is less for this shield, it is a far better shield overall.

The Watts 4 Dinner shield has the ability Overshield Eater, which makes it so enemies have an 8% chance to drop an overshield when hit. Whenever you have an overshield active, you get a bonus 25% shock damage.

This is very easy to obtain, especially if you have skills on your character that grant overshield. Giving you a consistent 25% damage bonus is amazing, making this shield one of the best in the game. You can get this shield by farming Origo in the Vault of Origo.

Nova shields can be really strong, especially when they give you a damage buff and also release a nova. The Cindershelly is great because it does both of these things, making it easy to take down enemies.

This shield has the Glass ability, which makes it so you get a stack of resolve whenever the shield is damaged. Each stack of resolve grants you 2% damage reduction, and when full of stacks, this means you have a 50% damage reduction.

To top it off, when this shield breaks, it releases a nova that deals a set amount of damage, but this damage is increased by 25% for each stack of resolve you have, meaning you can do an insane amount of damage with the blast. You can get this shield from The Backhive in Dissected Plateau.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

#4247. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

#4246. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, then check out our list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks we wish we knew before starting the game. Then check out our breakdown of the requirements to see the best ending in the game.

#4244. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4243. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4241. Off the AppStore: Bless the fans, bless Undertale Vs Gojo

Welcome to Off The AppStore, a weekly feature with a twist. Namely, while these - as with all the games we cover here - are games that you can play on your phone, they're ones that operate outside of the realms of the big two ways to play: The Google Play Store and the Apple AppStore.

That means that there might be a bit of work required in downloading alternative AppStores or  APKs, or that the games can simply be played in your phone browser. We'll make sure to detail that for each game, though. Anyway, read on to find a new game or experience to play Off The AppStore.

SPOILERS! This may be one of the few times I must protect your delicate little eyes from the secrets I'm about to reveal. Before we get to that, let's first talk about fans. If you like something, you're a fan. Don't blame me, blame the dictionary, or society if you want an easy target. While some fans can be insufferable constructs of cringe, others get inspired by what they like and make something only they can make. They want to share their passion with us in whatever way they know how. Gatolinie is one such fan (of TWO things, oh my god, so wild) and has brought us their fanfiction in the form of Undertale Vs Gojo.

Let's break it down: Undertale is a pixel indie RPG made by Toby Fox in 2015 that is considered one of the weirdest, most emotional, and best RPGs of all time. Then there's Satoru Gojo, an overpowered Japanese heartthrob from the anime Jujutsu Kaisen. Now, what if the main character from Undertale (Frisk) and Gojo decided to fight? Well, there's a high chance that an entire reality will break into pieces. But it's not that simple… You have to win the fight first.

You play as the version of Frisk who has gone down the path of violence, killing every monster and character they've come across, essentially becoming the villain. After defeating one of the game's hardest bosses, you come across Satoru Gojo, ripped from his universe and dropped into your path. He's in your way, and you decide that the only way through is with violence. Of course, as an anime mentor character, Gojo is exceptionally fast and strong, with a power that literally prevents any attack from touching him. This will be a difficult fight, and Gojo will give you everything he's got.

Undertale Vs Satoru Gojo is a 2D pixel RPG fan game about using Undertale mechanics to fight one of the most popular and powerful anime characters. A lot of effort went into the animations for Gojo, his attacks, and the Undertale UI to blend these two worlds as seamlessly as possible. It's short but challenging, and don't expect to beat it on your first try. You're encouraged to keep going just to talk to Gojo some more, see more of his attacks, and see if you can still come out on top.

Undertale Vs Gojo is available to download and play from its itch.io page!

#4240. Bill & Ted Sidescroller to Launch Backerkit Campaign in 2027

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

For the uninitiated, Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure was a 1989 sci-fi comedy starring Alex Winter and Keanu Reeves as the titular duo of teenage weirdos who get a chance to travel through time, meet famous historical figures, and make mild nuisances of themselves. It also co-starred my personal hero and one of the greatest comedians of all time, the late George Carlin, as their host in a time-traveling phone booth, Rufus.

The film, as well as its two sequels, remains one of the hallmarks of late 80s, early 90s pop culture, with any proclamation of “excellent” being a great way to make millennials spontaneously start air guitar-ing. Outside its films, the IP pops up in mildly odd places every now and then, including, apparently, a brand-new video game.

Spider-Man's video game adaptations are just as wild and varied as his comic book counterpart's adventures.

Indie developer Art of Play Interactive announced today that it’s developing a brand-new Bill & Ted game, Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure Arcade, a hybrid sidescrolling beat ‘em up and minigame collection based on the first film. This game is slated to be bankrolled by a Backerkit campaign, which is planned to launch in February 2027 with a handful of physical rewards available for early backers, as well as presently unannounced other swag like collectibles and apparel.

According to the game’s Backerkit and Steam pages, Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure Arcade is meant to be a playable version of the original film, starting with Rufus whisking the boys away into history in the time-traveling phone booth and running them through 15 levels as they try to meet famous folks for their history report. The game will feature audio from Alex Winter, Keanu Reeves, and George Carlin ripped directly from the film’s original recordings. It’s all original stuff, by the way; the Backerkit page stresses that this project will not use any generative AI whatsoever.

Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure Arcade is meant to be a playable version of the original film.

The actual game seems to switch off between side-scrolling beat ‘em up and assorted minigames. Bill and Ted travel through the time periods, getting into scuffles or running away from them, and when they encounter a famous historical figure, you play minigames to earn their trust and get them to come with you, such as battling Beethoven in a music duel or beating Napoleon in an ice cream-eating contest.

Sébastien Benard's action roguelike has resurfaced with a release window after several years of radio silence.

The game is meant to be played in local co-op, one character per player, though you can also play it solo and assume control over both Bill and Ted simultaneously. After beating the game’s main story, you’ll unlock arcade mode for faster playthroughs, as well as the individual mini-games for piecemeal enjoyment.

As you often see for these kinds of campaigns, and especially those for popular IPs from the 80s, the Backerkit campaign for Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure Arcade is planned to be accompanied by assorted physical rewards for those who get in on the ground floor.

To start, everyone who backs the campaign will receive a free Rufus Metallic Phone Booth card; those who reserve their pledge for $5 will receive additional Bill and Ted metallic cards, and everyone who backs in the first 48 hours will receive a fourth metallic card featuring the “historical dudes.” These four cards can be built together with the included top and bottom pieces to create your own little phone booth model. According to the Backerkit page, there will be additional incentives during the campaign proper, including exclusive merch, apparel, and other goodies.

The game is aiming for digital release on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam. Additionally, the game will have a limited physical release, with boxes for the Switch and PS5 versions, and even a physical CD-ROM for the PC version. There also seems to be a knock-off SNES cartridge in the works, though I’m assuming it’s just a prop and won’t actually run on a SNES.

Open-world games are the norm for AAA developers, but games funded on Kickstarter can deliver immersive open-worlds too.

#4236. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4235. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s second seed. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Every team that plays at the 2027 Game Changers Championship will receive a payment equal to Gentle Mates’ runners-up prize this year. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

But, there's even bigger news on the horizon, as Guild Wars Reforged will also see the debut of the original Guild Wars' first DLC in over 20 years! Guild Wars Afterlife debuts January 13th 2027, with a suite of new content to enjoy.

Guild Wars Afterlife offers a pretty stunning change of scenery too, with adventurers stepping through the Mists of Tyria and into the brand-new land of Xotecha. This South American-inspired jungle realm seems to be very different to what players of Guild Wars have experienced so far.

Yes, you heard that right, a roguelike experience complete with a selection of different skills and various upgrades that carry over to each run. It's definitely an unusual change for an MMORPG that's otherwise been quite typical such as Guild Wars.

And I think that's the most interesting part of Guild Wars Afterlife. For many of us who didn't grow up with the original, it's a great reason to give it a go. But I can't help but wonder what fans of Guild Wars back in the day thing of such a radical new addition so many years later. We'll just have to see how it's received when Guild Wars Afterlife arrives in 2027!

Guild Wars Reforged is undoubtedly one of the grandest returns of an old hit to mobile. But if you're looking for other examples of great releases to play, why not check out our list of the best mobile games like World of Warcraft to see some of our choice picks you can play right now?

#4233. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

#4232. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4231. XBOX Confirms What Everyone Knew About The Elder Scrolls 6

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

Elder Scrolls 6 has been the talk of the town for months, with whispers of announcements and gameplay showcases constantly circulating. Bethesda has been resting on its laurels for quite a while now, using adaptations and remakes to buy time while they work on new entries in both of their flagship franchises.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

Still partnered with and owned by XBOX, the title of Bethesda’s newest fantasy epic has been a bit of an open secret, one finally confirmed by the biggest names at XBOX. In a Twitter post, Asha Sharma herself announced the title of Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. Continuing the theme of subtitles marking the game’s major locale, it’s easy to assume ES6 will take place in the capital of the same name.

Elder Scrolls 6 won’t be the first time series long players have entered the opulent city of Sentinel, as the desert-flanked capital also appeared in Elder Scrolls Online, and as far back as the original The Elder Scrolls: Arena.

Sentinel has a rich history for both players and the setting itself, standing apart as a city flanked by opposites, in both politics and environment. The split between ocean and desert does wonders to make it feel truly fantastical, while Bethesda has taken care to use real-world analogues to make the title location feel genuine.

After Skyrim’s focus on ice-cold mountains and Norse-themed culture, the Redguard housing Sentinel is set to be a major visual shift, one primed to breathe new life into the franchise. Bethesda is kind of playing with fire here, as many are expecting Sentinel to be an absolute blockbuster rivaling Skyrim’s universal acclaim.

With a new location to explore, one deeply ingrained in the lore and worldbuilding of The Elder Scrolls as a whole, Sentinel has the potential to be Bethesda’s biggest game ever, especially since the new Fallout is being handled by the team at Obsidian. With all their cards on the table, Bethesda are remaining remarkably tight-lipped, only unveiling the proper subtitle on their time, even when most already knew it.

There’s a respect to be paid for the adherence to their own schedule, but they’ll need to keep a tight ship. If Grand Theft Auto 6 has been any indication, there are individuals willing to hard focus on leaking major titles if the opportunity presents itself, and if proper gameplay or story spoilers manage to leak, I don’t think Bethesda will be able to stick their heads in the sand and wait it out.

For many, despite its age, Skyrim is still the archetypal fantasy RPG, a showcase of everything the general public wants out of the subgenre. Magic, monsters, and wild opportunities to help define both the setting and player character as an individual are all expectations they’ll need to meet, primed with experience and feedback from their latest attempts.

Elder Scrolls 6 won’t be the first time series long players have entered the opulent city of Sentinel, as the desert-flanked capital also appeared in Elder Scrolls Online, and as far back as the original The Elder Scrolls: Arena.

After the crash and burn of their most recent RPG attempt, Starfield, Bethesda needs to redeem themselves in the eyes of the general public, even as remasters like Oblivion and drops like Doom: The Dark Ages buy them time. It’s so exciting to think about one of the titans of the RPG genre returning to form, but it’s a little hard to be blindly optimistic.

Bethesda's hopes for the next generation are all riding off the back of Elder Scrolls Sentinel. Maybe a return to such an established region will give them the flow state they need to win back the gaming public while putting out their best work. The devil you know, after all.

#4229. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.

#4228. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4227. The Pokémon Company Is Counting Down To A Mysterious Date On Social Media

The Pokémon Company is no stranger to a little over-hyping every now and then, but its latest bit of marketing has us seriously thinking that there is a big announcement in the pipeline.

You see, TPC is counting down to... something. As brought to our attention by Serebii's Joe Merrick, the company has been sharing images on social media of its 30th anniversary icons, with a number underneath. Interestingly, these numbers decrease by the number of hours that have passed between each post — 1,025 on 18th October, 843 on 26th, 676 today.

Keeping the countdown going, this means that we'll hit zero on 30th November at 2pm UTC (thanks for doing the maths there, Joe!). The latest post even came with a full message under the logo, roughly translating to "Continue with Pokémon".

Confirmation. We have a third data point 676 hours from now is 14:00 UTC on November 30th 2026. As I predicted, they are counting down to then. What will arrive at that point, it remains a mystery.

Hmm. The big question is, what's this all about? 2pm UTC sure feels like the right time for a big announcement (it's when most eyes, worldwide, will be on it), and we can't imagine that TPC would put this much planning into something inconsequential.

What is it, then? Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire were rumoured to be coming to NSO last month, could it be that? Is it time we got another look at Winds and Waves, perhaps with a fire release date attached? Is there another full Pokémon Presents around the corner? Only time will tell, but it sure is an exciting prospect.

We'll be keeping an eye on the countdown throughout November and will let you know when any major news comes out of it.
